explanation: Count zeros separately and multiply nonzero entries with arbitrary-precision arithmetic. With no zeros, divide out each possible excluded factor; one zero permits only its exclusion to produce a nonzero answer, while two zeros force zero.
spaceComplexity: O(B), where B is the bit length of the product
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Without zeros, dividing the full nonzero product by each entry evaluates exactly every allowed exclusion. With one zero, excluding another entry leaves product zero while excluding that zero gives the nonzero product. With two or more zeros every exclusion still leaves a zero. Taking the maximum among these exhaustive possibilities is optimal.
walkthrough: For [−2,3,−4,2], the full product is 48. Excluding entries in order gives −24, 16, −12 and 24, so the greatest n−1-entry product is 24.
edgeCases: Two or more zeros force a zero result.
One zero may be best excluded, depending on the sign of the other product.
Arbitrary-precision intermediates avoid product overflow before the int result.
